description:
The in-memory storage backend holds a redo record as a value and applies it by stepping through the same interruption points as the filesystem backend.

## Background

The in-memory backend exists so command workflows are testable without a filesystem, and the project requires one behavioural contract across both backends. The in-memory session mirrors the filesystem kernel today by walking the same failure points in the same order over an in-memory residue, with one deliberately skipped step marked so the point set stays identical across backends.

The redo record keeps that shape and shrinks it. The in-memory backend stores the record as a value beside its state map, applies its operations to that map in the same order, and checks the same interruption points, so a crash injected at a given point means the same thing on both backends. The residue carries the record alone.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A mutation on the in-memory backend installs a redo record as a value before it changes any state entry.
- [hard] REQ-02: Applying the record updates put entries, removes delete entries, and extends the event entry at its recorded offset.
- [hard] REQ-03: Re-applying a leftover record over a backend that already holds part of it leaves the backend in the same semantic state as a clean application.
- [hard] REQ-04: The backend checks the same interruption-point values, in the same order, as the filesystem backend, and each point is reachable on both.
- [hard] REQ-05: The in-memory residue carries the record and nothing else.

## Notes

Expected additive footprint is under 200 production lines, against roughly 340 lines of kernel modelling this replaces.


## Non-goals

No publisher commits through the record in this task. The in-memory mutation session still publishes through its existing failure-point choreography, and the repository's observable publication behaviour is unchanged; `4319256e` (session commit through the redo record) is where a mutation's apply begins committing through the record, and `b0ee2dd6` (transaction kernel retirement) is where the kernel's own residue and its modelling are removed — plan decision LD-11 places that retirement in the cutover phase. REQ-01 and REQ-05 are properties of the record path this task adds: the backend installs the record before it changes any state entry on that path, and the record residue this task introduces carries the record and nothing else. The mechanism is built and proven beside the one in use, which is what story `21e976d1` REQ-03 requires of every task in this phase.
title: Memory-backend record application
